diagnostic_evidence.quote: As shown in the proof of Theorem \ref{t-lasso:general-approximation-theorem-main}, we now consider the upper bound for $\|\widetilde{\mathbf{A}}-\mathbf{A}\|_{\max}$

issues.failure_explanation: By the stated Parseval identity, the L^2 norm of sum (A-EF*)(i1,i2) e^{i(k1x1+k2x2)} equals ||A-EF*||_F. That can exceed ||A-EF*||_max by a factor of up to sqrt((2I1+1)(2I2+1)). The max-norm guarantee of Theorem t-lasso:epsilonrank-main therefore only gives sqrt((2I1+1)(2I2+1)) eps||A||_2. The stated bound is false: take A an identity block of size R+1 at low modes, so |f|_alpha is fixed. Any rank-R surrogate then has Frobenius error >=1, while the right side tends to eps<1 as I grows. Corollary cor:added-1 combines the max-norm CUR bound with the same step.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must bound ||A-EF*||_F (e.g. via Eckart-Young tail singular values or a Frobenius-norm CUR bound). This abandons the logarithmic-rank max-norm guarantee, or multiplies the eps-term by sqrt((2I1+1)(2I2+1)).
issues.overall_effect: The central guarantee (L^2 accuracy eps||A||_2 with rank R=O(log(I1+I2)/eps^2)) and the max-volume CUR L^2 bound are unsupported. The correct bound degrades by about 2 sqrt(I1 I2), roughly 6300 for the paper's I=3163.
issues.title: L^2 error of the low-rank surrogate bounded by the max-norm instead of the Frobenius norm
issues.why_classification: The advertised rank/accuracy trade-off is lost: a correct version needs a different norm and loses the log-rank guarantee, with a polynomial-in-I degradation.

issues.failure_explanation: With k=0 the first block is T'=[0:b-1] U [-b+1:0], which repeats the index 0 already in T={0}. C and R then get duplicated columns and rows, so sigma_min=0 and tol=0 at once, and G=C(T1+I1+1,:) no longer matches R(:,T2+I2+1) in shape. issues.title: Loop control of the adaptive algorithms is broken (k=0 duplicates index 0; 'or' ignores K; min vs max criterion)
issues.why_classification: Local pseudocode corrections restore the intended procedure without changing the method or its counts.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For clarity, we set that $\alpha=2$, $C=1$, $\epsilon=1e-7$ and $|f(x_1,x_2)|_{\alpha}=1$.
Let $f(\cdot,\cdot)$ be a continuous periodic function of two variables

issues.failure_explanation: f2(pi,x2) differs from f2(-pi,x2), and f3 is likewise non-periodic, so their periodic extensions are discontinuous and not in H^alpha for alpha>=1/2. The kink function f1 has first-derivative jumps, so |f1|_2 is infinite. Setting alpha=2 and |f|_alpha=1 therefore uses Theorem t-lasso:general-theorem-main outside its hypotheses, and the implied accuracy 1e-7 is unjustified for all three tests.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use periodic test functions with known Sobolev regularity, or compute I_n from the actual regularity and seminorm, and rerun the comparisons.
issues.overall_effect: The experimental parameter choice and its implied accuracy have no theoretical basis; the 'Truncated Fourier' baseline is not an eps-accurate reference.
issues.title: Truncation order derived from Theorem 3.1 with alpha=2 for test functions not in H^2 (two not even periodic)
issues.why_classification: The experimental setup must be redone, but the methods themselves are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Under this case, $Ff(x_1,x_2)$ can be viewed as a special case for the hyperinterpolation of $f(x_1,x_2)$ onto the subspace generated by

issues.failure_explanation: Hyperinterpolation requires a rule exact for products of basis functions, here frequencies up to 2I_n=6326. The equispaced periodic rule with 5001 points aliases e^{ikx} with e^{i(k-5001)x}. For k>=1838 both lie in [-3163,3163], e.g. k=2000 and -3001, so discrete orthogonality fails and the computed coefficients are aliased. CC and GL rules with 5001 nodes are not trigonometrically exact either.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose M_n >= 2I_n+1 (trapezoidal rule), or reduce I_n to below M_n/2, and rerun the experiments.
issues.overall_effect: The computed coefficients are not the hyperinterpolation (or Fourier) coefficients of the stated truncation, which undermines the numerical accuracy comparisons.
issues.title: Quadrature with M=5001 points cannot integrate frequencies up to 2I=6326; hyperinterpolation exactness fails
issues.why_classification: Parameter consistency must be restored and the experiments recomputed; the method is untouched.

issues.failure_explanation: With G=blockdiag(G_0,...,G_K) and U=G^dagger, C U R = sum_k A(:,T2k) A(T1k,T2k)^dagger A(T1k,:). Take A=u v^T with nonzero blocks, e.g. f=e^{cos x1} e^{cos x2}, whose Fourier coefficients are all positive. Each term then equals A exactly, so the output is (K+1)A. issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must use the true intersection submatrix (or a justified consistent core) in place of the zero off-diagonal blocks, which reverts to Algorithm 2.
